title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages). We start from an exact sequence (27): 1 → M → G → H → 1. Here G is a discrete group, M is a normal subgroup that is a free Z-module of finite type, and H acts on M by conjugation.

Over a base S0 (apparently Spec Z, or a connected base) Grothendieck builds a sheaf of groups G̲ (the underlined G). It contains the vector group M̲ = M ⊗_Z O_S as a normal subgroup, with quotient the constant group H_{S0}. It also comes with a homomorphism φ : G_{S0} → G̲ from the constant group scheme, under which M_{S0} is the inverse image of M̲. This is the content of (35)–(36).

What this page says.
- Eq. (38): by construction there is a commutative diagram of exact sequences of group sheaves. The top row is 1 → M_{S0} → G_{S0} → H_{S0} → 1, the bottom row is 1 → M̲ → G̲ → H_{S0} → 1, and the right-hand vertical arrow is the identity.
- Eq. (39): taking sections over an affine S = Spec A gives a commutative diagram with rows 1 → M → G → H → 1 and 1 → M⊗_Z A → G̲(A) → H → 1. Surjectivity onto H uses the vanishing of H^1(S, M⊗O_S), as noted on the previous page.
- For S = S0 one recovers the isomorphism (28), presumably G̲(Z) ≅ G.
- In modern terms, G̲(A) is the pushout of the extension (27) along the H-equivariant map M → M⊗A. Concretely, G̲(A) = ((M⊗A) ⋊ G) / {(m, m⁻¹)}. The class in H²(H, M) is simply pushed to H²(H, M⊗A).
- Eqs. (40)–(41): the construction is manifestly functorial in the extension (27). A morphism of extensions induces a morphism of the associated diagrams; the next page draws this as a cube.
- Margin NB: in sheaf language on S, G̲ is an extension of the constant sheaf H by M⊗_Z O_S, obtained from G by 'tensoring the kernel'.

Purpose. This is a 'linearization' of the abelian kernel: the extension is made into a family over Spec Z whose fibres interpolate G over A = Q, Z_ℓ, F_p, and so on. The next page turns to finite-index sublattices M_i ⊂ M, giving finite quotients G/M_i, and mentions an 'N-adinisation' of discrete solvable groups. This fits Grothendieck's programme in the Longue Marche continuation of comparing discrete groups (e.g. surface/braid-type groups, or extensions by lattices) with their profinite and ℓ-adic or 'adinised' completions.
errors: No real error. Surjectivity G̲(A) → H for affine S requires H^1(S, M⊗O_S) = 0 (or triviality of the relevant torsors). Grothendieck flags this himself on the previous page and in the inserted remark.
The identification at S = S0 with (28) needs S0 = Spec Z, or at least A = Z with Spec A connected so that constant-scheme sections equal G. This is implicit, not stated.

ideas.what: Group sheaf G̲ over Spec Z obtained by pushing out an extension 1→M→G→H→1 with M a free Z-module along M → M⊗O_S, compatible with the constant group scheme G_{S0}
ideas.modern_name: pushout of a group extension along a coefficient change; a (very elementary) relative/partial Malcev-type completion relative to the quotient H
ideas.usually_credited_to: pushout of extensions: classical (Eilenberg–MacLane / Baer). Relative (Malcev) completion as a systematic tool: Deligne, Hain (late 1980s–1990s)
ideas.where_published: Longue Marche (1981) discusses discrete versus profinite extensions; this specific schematic construction is not known to appear there

ideas.what: Functoriality of the construction in the extension (diagrams (40)–(41))

missed.claim: Grothendieck treats a discrete extension with free abelian kernel as the Z-points of a group sheaf over Spec Z whose A-points are the kernel-linearized extensions. This is a schematic family interpolating rational, ℓ-adic and mod-p versions. It foreshadows the relative completion relative to H (Hain), in the special case of an abelian kernel. The next page then announces an 'N-adinisation' of discrete solvable groups. The construction is elementary, so novelty is small; at most it documents his early interest in such interpolations.
missed.quote: Cette construction du faisceau en groupes G̲, à partir d'une suite exacte (27), est manifestement fonctorielle
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically of interest as an unpublished Grothendieck precursor to relative completions and 'adinisation' of solvable or polycyclic groups. Mathematically routine.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is a standard pushout of an extension, phrased sheaf-theoretically over Spec Z. It is interesting only as context for an unpublished programme on adinising discrete solvable groups, which is visible on the next page rather than this one.
transcription_corrections: Line 'pour S quelconque affine' reads more as: 'qui par passage aux sections donne, pour S affine (disons), un diagramme commutatif' ('pour' and 'quelconque' are struck through).
After 'S=S_0 on retrouve l'iso (28)' the next word (on its own line) is probably 'annoncé' or 'mentionné'.
The group symbol is Grothendieck's script G (𝔊), consistent with the G of the neighbouring pages. The underlined G̲ and M̲ denote sheaves over S0.
Margin note: roughly 'NB En termes de faisceaux sur S, on a une structure de faisceau en groupes G̲ ... extension de H par M̲ ... isomorphisme ... M ⊗_Z O_S'. The exact wording is uncertain.
